scenes.say: This tiny animal survived open space.
scenes.cap: This tiny animal SURVIVED open SPACE.

scenes.say: It's a tardigrade. A water bear. About half a millimeter long.
scenes.cap: It's a TARDIGRADE. A water bear. About HALF A MILLIMETER long.

scenes.say: It lives almost everywhere. In moss, on mountains, in the deep sea.
scenes.cap: It lives almost EVERYWHERE. In moss, on mountains, in the deep sea.

scenes.say: When life gets hard, it dries out, and curls into a ball called a tun.
scenes.cap: When life gets hard, it DRIES OUT, and curls into a ball called a TUN.

scenes.say: Like this, it has survived cold close to absolute zero.
scenes.cap: Like this, it has survived cold close to ABSOLUTE ZERO.

scenes.say: And heat hotter than boiling water, for a few minutes.
scenes.cap: And heat HOTTER than boiling water, for a few minutes.

scenes.say: And radiation hundreds of times stronger than a deadly human dose.
scenes.cap: And RADIATION hundreds of times stronger than a deadly human dose.

scenes.say: In two thousand seven, scientists sent them to space, outside the spacecraft, for ten days.
scenes.cap: In 2007, scientists sent them to SPACE, outside the spacecraft, for 10 DAYS.

scenes.say: Many survived. Some even laid eggs that hatched.
scenes.cap: Many SURVIVED. Some even laid EGGS that hatched.

scenes.say: Just add water, and it wakes back up.
scenes.cap: Just add WATER... and it WAKES back up.

upload.title: This Animal Survived Space 🐻 #shorts
upload.description:
Tardigrades (water bears) are about half a millimetre long. Dried out into a 'tun', they can survive extreme cold, heat and radiation. In 2007, on the FOTON-M3 mission, tardigrades spent 10 days exposed to open space - and many survived.

Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tardigrade
